title: A rejecting reviewer attaches a concrete fix for every open finding, and the next round is reviewed by someone else
public_title: Attach a fix to every open review finding
acceptance: Why. When a reviewer rejects a pull request today, it writes what is wrong but not how to fix it. firstmate then sends a separate agent to reproduce each finding, find the cause and write a brief for the next worker round. A reported observation from the 2026-10-09 firstmate session, not a measured benchmark: that diagnosis step took roughly 10 to 30 minutes per round, while the following worker round often finished in a few minutes (T-242 rounds 5 and 6, T-264 round 5). The reviewer has already read the whole diff, so it is the cheapest place to ask for the fix. We keep reviewers read-only: a reviewer that edited and committed code would be reviewing its own work, which breaks the independent approval that gate 6 (the approval gate) depends on.

Terms. A 'fix proposal' is the reviewer's concrete answer to one open finding: either a patch in unified diff format against the reviewed head, or, when a patch is impractical, an exact description of the change. The 'standing list' is the numbered list that every REJECT ends with, closed by `CRITERIA-COMPLETE:<task-id>` (design/design.md section 7). An 'open item' is a standing-list item whose first line starts with `open` (optionally bold), or, in a list with no earlier standing list for the task, any item whose first line does not start with `done`. A REGRESSION or NEW-GROUND item is open. The existing done/open state rules for later lists do not change.

Change 1, reviewer rule. skills/reviewer/SKILL.md, section 'Every REJECT closes its list', gains this rule: every open item in a REJECT's standing list carries exactly one fix proposal or exactly one decision line (Change 3). Reviewers stay read-only and never commit, push or edit files. The rule applies to code review only, not to spec preflight. An APPROVE needs no fix proposals.

Change 2, fix proposal format. A fix proposal is a fenced block whose info string is `diff fix-<N>` (a patch) or `text fix-<N>` (a description), where <N> is an open item's number. A patch block holds a non-empty unified diff with `a/` and `b/` paths relative to the repository root. A text block holds four labelled lines, each with non-empty text: `file:` (path and line), `change:`, `fixes:` (the failing assertion it fixes) and `fail-first:` (the assertion it expects to fail on the old code for a real reason).

Change 2, exactly one. Each of these is a protocol error naming the item: two or more fix blocks for the same <N>; a fix block plus a decision line for the same <N>; two or more DECISION lines for the same <N>, even with identical questions; an empty patch; a text block missing a labelled line or with an empty one; a fix block or DECISION line whose <N> is not an open item of the same standing list.

Change 3, decisions instead of patches. When an open item needs a decision only the captain can make, for example a conflict between spec and code, or a fix that needs a path outside the task's pinned scope, the reviewer writes, as an indented continuation line inside that item, `DECISION:<task-id> <question>` with the item's own task ID and a non-empty question. A DECISION line with another task ID, an empty question, or no indentation is not a decision line. Whether a fix needs an out-of-scope path is the reviewer's judgment; the machine additionally reports patch paths outside the pinned scope (Change 7) but does not refuse them.

Change 4, the review prompt. bin/fm-review.sh prints the fix-proposal instruction in every review round, round one included: one line after the existing closing instruction that says each open item needs a `fix-<N>` block or an indented `DECISION:<task-id>` line, and that reviewers do not edit files. Today closed_list runs only from round two (`bin/fm-review.sh` around line 876), so the new line is printed outside closed_list. closed_list, its ASK clarification and its existing sentences stay as they are.

Change 5, parsing. bin/lib/fm_evidence.py gains a function `fixes(text, task)` that reads fix proposals from a verdict's raw text. It does not use unquoted(), which drops fenced blocks. It counts only fenced blocks and DECISION lines that sit between the first item of the final standing list (the block criteria() selects) and the `CRITERIA-COMPLETE:<task-id>` line; quoted examples, earlier lists and text after the closing marker are ignored. It returns, per item number, the proposal kind (patch, text or decision), its content, and a list of errors. It writes nothing to standard output.

Change 6, protocol check. protocol() in bin/lib/fm_evidence.py appends the Change 2 errors and `open item <N> has no fix proposal or DECISION` for every REJECT record that carries `fix_protocol: 1` (Migration). `bin/fm-protocol.sh check` therefore exits 3 for such a verdict, with the same diagnostic and event path it uses today.

Change 6, autopilot runs the check first. Both REJECT branches in bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py (the advance path near line 392 and the completed-review path near line 618) run the protocol check for the REJECT's round before anything else, in every round, round one included. The check is bound to the triggering REJECT: bin/fm-protocol.sh and `fm_evidence protocol` gain `--signature <verdict signature>`, which judges the standing-list sequence up to and including that record and ignores later records, so a later record cannot mask the triggering error while earlier lists still give context. Without `--signature` both behave exactly as today. On failure the autopilot raises the existing protocol-violation wake with its English and Traditional Chinese text and stops. On success they continue with Change 9. After a restart, the same poll repeats the check and reaches the same result; the existing once-per-head wake key prevents a second wake for the same head.

Change 7, patches are checked before the verdict is stored. retain_verdict in bin/lib/fm_evidence.py, before its single store.append, runs a check for every patch block in the exact answer text it is about to retain (for codex, the authenticated final answer). The check is read-only: it reads the reviewed head into a temporary Git index file (`GIT_INDEX_FILE=<temp> git read-tree <head>`) in the target repository and runs `git apply --cached --check` against it, so it needs no checkout and works in both review modes. It deletes the temporary index afterwards and changes no tracked file, ref or worktree.

Change 7, the stored result. The verdict record gains one field `fix_checks` with this JSON shape: `{"version": 1, "status": "complete" | "unavailable", "reason": <text or null>, "items": {"<N>": {"kind": "patch" | "text" | "decision", "apply": "applies" | "does-not-apply" | "not-a-patch", "message": <Git's first error line or null>, "outside_scope": [<patch paths matching no glob of the pinned scope>]}}}`. Applicability and outside-scope are separate fields, so an out-of-scope patch still reports whether it applies. If the check cannot run (Git missing, a 60-second timeout, a read error), status is `unavailable` with a reason, items is empty, and the verdict is still retained. Readers treat an absent field (legacy) or an `unavailable` status as 'patch check unavailable', and a missing item entry as 'patch check missing for item <N>'. The temporary index lives in a new directory created with the system temporary-directory facility (Python tempfile), never under the target repository or the engine root, and is removed in a finally block. The repository's real index file, refs and worktree are not touched. If the process is killed before the append, no verdict is retained, as today, and the repository is unchanged. A patch that does not apply is not a protocol error. The record is signed once, as today; the launcher's evidence reference (the signature) is unchanged.

Change 8, the brief draft. bin/lib/fm_evidence.py gains a command `fixes-brief --round <next round> --head <head>`. It reads, through the existing Store.verdicts() (and so the existing FM_REVIEWER_LOGIN filter), the latest verdict record whose verdict is REJECT and whose head equals <head>. <next round> must equal that record's round plus one. It exits 65 with a message, writing nothing, when there is no such record, when <next round> does not match, when the record has no `fix_protocol: 1` (a legacy verdict), or when its fixes have protocol errors. Otherwise it writes the draft to `<project state>/briefs/<task>-r<next round>-<first 12 characters of head>-<first 8 characters of the verdict signature>-review-fixes.md`, where <project state> is the selected project's private state directory that Store already uses (self: state/; external: the private project state), never the target checkout. It prints that path.

Change 8, draft content. For each standing-list item in order the draft has one line. An open item gets `<N>. fix: <first line of the finding>`, then its fix proposal copied byte for byte in a fenced block, then its `fix_checks` result. A decision item gets `<N>. deferred: captain decision needed: <question>`. A done item gets `<N>. deferred: done in the reviewed round; keep as is`. A missing or unavailable check shows as 'patch check unavailable' or 'patch check missing for item <N>'. A last line names the reviewer actor, the verdict's round, head and signature. Because the file name binds the head and the source verdict, a different head or a corrected verdict gets a new file and never reuses an old draft. If the file for the same head and verdict already exists, the command does not overwrite it and prints its path, so firstmate's appended context survives a repeat call.

Change 9, firstmate records the draft. When the protocol check passes, the autopilot runs `fixes-brief`. When it succeeds and no item is a decision, the wake is `<task> REJECT: review fixes ready at <path relative to the project state>; record the brief` in English and `<task> 審查拒絕：審查修正草稿已備好於 <同一路徑>；請記錄工作簡報` in Traditional Chinese. For an external project the wake omits the path and says only that the draft is in the private project state. When fixes-brief fails or a decision item exists, the wake stays the existing 'REJECT: brief needed' text. firstmate reads the draft, may append a section titled 'Context from firstmate' with facts the reviewer lacked, does not change the copied proposals, and records it with the existing `fm-evidence brief` command for the exact round and head. skills/firstmate/SKILL.md rule 6 (a worker round gets a brief, not a symptom) says this.

Change 10, the draft passes the existing coverage check. Because every item, done and open, has a `<N>. fix:` or `<N>. deferred:` line, the reject coverage check in bin/lib/fm_context_pack.py, which needs one of those per finding, reports no gap. That file does not change. A test feeds a generated draft for a mixed done/open/decision list to that check.

Change 11, two-person rule. The review round after a REJECT is reviewed by a different reviewer name. bin/fm-review.sh, in review mode only, reads the latest REJECT verdict record for the task and passes that record's reviewer name to allocation as the avoided name (for example through an environment variable such as FM_AVOID_REVIEWER). choose_name in bin/fm-herdr.py excludes the avoided name from the automatic choice, including when it is the task's last reviewer name. A retry of the same round keeps its own name unless that name is the avoided one. An explicit `--name` equal to the avoided name is refused with a clear message. When no other reviewer name is free, the existing 'roster ran out' error applies. Workers and spec preflight pass no avoided name and keep their behaviour.

Change 12, history for the new reviewer. The next reviewer receives the prior standing list and earlier verdicts through the existing local history, filtered exactly as today: with FM_REVIEWER_LOGIN unset (the stock default) it gets every earlier verdict whatever its own name is; with FM_REVIEWER_LOGIN set, the existing login filter applies unchanged. A test covers a rotated reviewer with the default; the existing login-filter test stays as is.

Migration. retain_verdict writes `fix_protocol: 1` on every verdict it retains after this change. protocol() applies the Change 6 rules only to records with that field, so verdicts retained before the change, including a round launched on the old frozen launcher that finishes after the change, are judged by the old rules. fixes-brief refuses a legacy REJECT, so the autopilot falls back to 'REJECT: brief needed'. Avoided-name rotation uses the reviewer name of the latest REJECT whether or not it has the field. Existing pins, briefs, verdict bytes and signatures are not rewritten. Tests cover: an old REJECT without fixes still passing protocol; a new one failing it; an old REJECT followed by a rotated next allocation; fixes-brief refusing a legacy REJECT; a review launched on the old frozen launcher that retains its verdict after the change (no fix_protocol field, judged by the old rules); an existing pin and an authorized brief recorded before the change keeping their bytes and signatures, with the exact round-and-head brief lookup still returning that brief.

External privacy. Fix proposals, patch-check messages and drafts stay in the selected project's private state. Under FM_EXTERNAL=1 a test proves that the draft lands in the private project state, that two projects with the same task ID do not see each other's drafts, and that no proposal text, Git message or private path appears in a wake, event summary or other public output.

Unchanged. The authenticated final-answer selector (T-163), standing-list numbering, done/open states, REGRESSION and NEW-GROUND labels, the CRITERIA-COMPLETE, APPROVE and REJECT markers, gate 6, the ASK-PASS-CRITERIA exception, the FM_REVIEWER_LOGIN filter, spec preflight, and reviewers' read-only sandbox.

Design. design/design.md section 7 (The standing list) gains, inside that section: the fix-proposal and decision rules, the protocol errors, the patch check and the brief draft. Section 11 gains one sentence in its paragraph about crew names (a name always means one role, T-104): the review round after a REJECT uses a different reviewer name.

Tests, new behaviour that fails on the current main for a behavioural reason (name each assertion in .fm-say.md): a new REJECT whose open item has no proposal fails protocol (main accepts it), including an unmarked first-round finding, while its counterpart with a valid proposal passes; each Change 2 error case fails protocol, including two identical DECISION lines; with `--signature`, a later valid record does not mask the triggering REJECT's error; a DECISION line that is unindented or names another task does not count; the round-one prompt contains the fix-proposal line (main prints none); the review after a REJECT gets a different reviewer name (main reuses the name); an explicit --name equal to the avoided name is refused; the autopilot wake names the draft and has both languages; a REJECT with protocol errors raises the protocol-violation wake in round one (main raises 'brief needed'); the protocol check and the wake run on both autopilot REJECT paths, and a restart produces no second wake for the same head; a retry of the round after a REJECT, where the previous round's reviewer name is free and would be chosen on main, still gets a different name; exclusion that leaves no free reviewer name raises 'roster ran out'.

Tests, new interface (absent on main, not counted as fail-first evidence): fixes() parsing, with cases for a quoted example before the list, an earlier list, text after the closing marker, an unknown item number and a fenced block that itself contains a CRITERIA-COMPLETE line, and proof that criteria() selects the same standing list as before; fixes-brief output, byte-for-byte proposals, refusal cases (no REJECT, wrong round, legacy, protocol errors), missing or unavailable check results, same-source repeat returning the same path, and changed-head and changed-verdict calls producing new files; a generated draft for a mixed done/open/decision list passing the coverage check in bin/lib/fm_context_pack.py; fix_checks values including does-not-apply, not-a-patch, paths-outside-scope and unavailable, and proof that the check changes no tracked file, ref or worktree; external privacy; the patch check's temporary index is created outside the target repository and the engine root for both a self and an external project and is gone afterwards, and the repository's index file hash, refs and worktree status are unchanged; an interruption injected during the check, before store.append, publishes no verdict record and no evidence-record.json mirror, and leaves existing record bytes, signatures and repository state unchanged. Compatibility tests that pass on main and must keep passing: a complete REJECT with valid proposals keeps its standing-list syntax valid; an ordinary retry of the same review round keeps its own name; history reaches a rotated reviewer with FM_REVIEWER_LOGIN unset, and with it set the existing login filter still applies to a rotated reviewer; handcrafted brief text with `<N>. fix:` and `<N>. deferred:` lines passes the coverage check; spec preflight allocation and the worker same-name case are unchanged. New files: tests/review-fixes.test.sh and tests/lib/review_fixes.py.

Tests, existing fixtures. Fixtures that retain a new REJECT through the live retain path get fix blocks so they stay green: tests/local-round-loop.test.sh (around lines 37 and 92), tests/e2e-loop.test.sh (around line 73), tests/review-evidence.test.sh (around lines 14 to 30) and tests/lib/local_round_records.py (around lines 101 to 118). Records those tests write directly as legacy history keep no fix_protocol field and stay as they are. tests/review-diff.test.sh updates its expected prompt only by the one added line of Change 4. tests/herdr/roster.py keeps test_second_round_keeps_the_first_rounds_name_when_free (a worker case) unchanged. tests/lib/autopilot_loop.py (around lines 212 to 218) has a REJECT case that expects an immediate 'brief needed' wake from a synthetic verdict; it is updated to supply a complete legacy verdict record and a successful protocol check, keeping its once-only wake and its no-worker and no-review assertions. That file already holds 1200 lines and must stay at or under 1200, so new autopilot cases go in tests/lib/review_fixes.py.

Overlap. T-270 (plain writing) also edits skills/reviewer/SKILL.md, skills/firstmate/SKILL.md, bin/fm-review.sh and bin/lib/fm_evidence.py. Whichever merges second rebases and keeps both rule sets: the reviewer list rules at skills/reviewer/SKILL.md section 'Every REJECT closes its list', firstmate rule 6, the prompt closing lines, and protocol().

Option-loop pin. This task adds one value-taking flag, `--signature`, to `bin/fm-protocol.sh`. `tests/option-loop.test.sh` pins every script's count of value-taking flags and the total number of probed cases, so it must change in exactly two places: the `fm-protocol` row goes from 5 to 6, and the total check goes from 123 to 124 (the assertion text says 124 too). Nothing else in that file changes. Test label: this is interface maintenance, not behavioural fail-first evidence. On the base the two pins already match (5 flags, 123 cases); they turn red only on this task's implementation head once `--signature` exists (seen on #261 head 06bbc28f, CI run 37948396086, shard 1), and the two edits make them pass again. The behavioural evidence for `--signature` stays the separately specified signature-bound protocol test. Note: T-270 (#260) also edits this file (the `fm-review` row, 9 to 11); whichever task merges later rebases, keeps both rows, and sets the total to the base's total plus its own added cases (123 + 1 here; 126 if T-270's two cases are already on the base).
